Thereafter, IO got to know about the ownership of the Tractor and served the notice u/s. 133 MV Act upon the owner of the offending vehicle. Owner produced the driver of the offending vehicle. Driver was arrested and was released on bail as the offence was bailable. Mechanical inspection of offending vehicle was got conducted and released on Superdari. Documents pertaining to the offending vehicle were got verified and they were found to be correct. Thereafter, IO submitted the MLC of the injured Ajay for final opinion and later, he collected the same. As per final opinion of MLC, the injury was 'simple'. On completion of investigation, chargesheet was filed against respondent no. 1, Sanjay Kachhi under Section 279/337/304A IPC and DAR was filed before this Tribunal.

5. Respondent nos. 1 and 2 did not file any written statement. Respondent no. 3 filed its reply.

FINDINGS & OBSERVATIONS 9. Before delving into the facts of the current case to decide the aforementioned issues, it is pertinent to highlight that it is firmly established in legal precedents that the proceedings conducted before the Claims Tribunal are in the nature of an inquiry. Further, procedural approach adopted by an accident claims' tribunal mirrors that of a civil court (National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt.
Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287). In civil proceedings, the establishment of facts hinges on a preponderance of probabilities, rather than being bound by the strict rules of evidence or the higher standard of beyond reasonable doubt, as required in criminal cases. The burden of proof in civil cases is lighter than in criminal cases, and the burden to decide claim petition under The Motor Vehicles Act is even lesser as compared to a civil litigation. In Bimla Devi & Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SC 530, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that negligence must be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view must be adopted in reaching a conclusion. 
10. Keeping in mind the aforementioned legal principle for adjudicating the present issue, this Tribunal has thoroughly gone through the testimony of the witnesses and all the material available on record. Also, careful consideration has been given to the arguments addressed by the Learned Counsels for all the parties.

and during the period of treatment in the hospital, his family members have to face tremendous harassment and mental pain and agony and the treatment of the deponent is still continues and subsists.

5 towards Burari Bye-pass, Delhi, respondent no. 1 suddenly turned the offending vehicle bearing no.
HR 55G3251 due to which, the tractor forcefully hit the divider and Pappu Bansal (now deceased)
and he himself fell down on the road and while he sustained grievous injuries, Pappu Bansal sustained fatal injuries.
13. PW-1 emphatically testified that the accident occurred due to the fault of the driver of the offending vehicle who was driving at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner. PW-1 has specifically deposed qua the driving of the offending vehicle bearing registration no. HR- 55G - 3251 by respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner. Respondent no. 1 has not filed any reply. 
Respondent no. 1 has not even examined himself to prove that he was not rash or negligent and as such adverse inference has to be drawn against him (reliance is placed on the judgments of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the cases of Teja Singh Vs Suman & Ors., MAC. APP. 1111/2018 & CM APPL.

Secondly, the fact of the accident has not been disputed and thus, it stand established that the accident did take place due to which the petitioner sustained injuries. 
14. Furthermore, in view of filing of DAR containing the chargesheet for the offences u/s 279/337/304A IPC and other relevant documents against respondent no. 1 and in terms of the judgment in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi,
respondent no. 1 Sanjay Kanchi (driver of the offending vehicle) is held to be negligent on the basis of preponderance of probabilities. 
From the DAR, it also stands established that the offending vehicle bearing registration no.

Ltd. vide Policy No. 243502/31/2019/7890 valid from 26.02.2019 to 25.02.2020. The factum of said insurance is also admitted by the respondent no.3 insurance company in its reply. 
The injury:
15. The injured Ajay was taken to Loknayak Hospital after the accident where he was treated vide MLC bearing no. 113692859 dated 15.12.2019. The alleged history has been mentioned to be road traffic accident, however, no opinion has been given as to the nature of the injury suffered by him. Even the petitioner has not filed any medical treatment on record to prove the nature of his injuries. While he has mentioned in his Form XIV that he was hospitalised for two months but there is nothing on record to prove the same. The MLC only mentions pain over left elbow and left wrist. No further injury, abrasion or fracture has been mentioned. Further, the IO has filed the chargesheet under section 337 IPC with respect to the present petitioner. Therefore,
in the absence of any additional evidence, it is held that the petitioner Ajay suffered Ajay (I)(Fir414/2019/Burari) vs Sanjay Kachhi (Oic) on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172781374/
6 simple injury in the accident in question. 
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom? 
(OPP.)
16. The petitioner is certainly entitled for compensation in view of the decision of issue No.1 above. 
To prove his claim, he deposed as under:-
"9 That at the time of accident, the deponent was 22 years old, possessing good health and sound mind and robust physique and was not suffering from any kind of ailment or addicted to any voice. 
Occupationally, the deponent/injured at the time of accident, the deponent was working as Beldar and earning for a sum of Rs. 20,000/- per month from the said work. But due to heavy impact, the entire activity of the deponent has come to standstill because the work of the deponent was beldari. 
10. That the deponent has spent Rs. 20,000/- on his medical treatment and Rs.
10,000/- on conveyance and Rs. 49,000/- on special diet. The deponent/injured is also entitled to get compensation of Rs. 5,00,000/-." 
17. The petitioner is claiming a total compensation to the tune of Rs. 15,28,943/- (as per form XIV)
from the respondents. I have considered the evidence on record and perused the entire record. 
Before proceeding further to decide the present issue, it would be apposite to encapsulate the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its guiding lamp post judgment for ascertaining just compensation in road vehicular injury cases. In the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors. (2011)
1 SCC 34, Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under:
"General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4. The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. 
The Court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. (See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D.
Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby Ajay (I)(Fir414/2019/Burari) vs Sanjay Kachhi (Oic) on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172781374/
7 - 1970 AC 467).
5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following :
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages) 
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. 
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). 
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i),
(ii)(a) and (iv)..."
18. In view of the above law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in injury cases, award needs to be passed only under heads of medical expenses, loss of earning during treatment period and damages for pain, suffering and trauma. 
Determination of Injuries and Duration of the Treatment: 
19. It would be appropriate to first ascertain the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner/ injured and duration of treatment as they need to be kept in mind while ascertaining the compensation under different applicable heads. It has already been determined above that the petitioner suffered simple injury in the accident in question. Further, his period of hospitalization has not been proved. 
Thus, his compensation is computed as follows:
Medical expenses:

8 20. The petitioner has claimed Rs. 20,000/- towards medical expenses, however, he has not filed any document on record to prove the same. Hence, the petitioner/ injured Ajay shall not be entitled to any amount towards medical expenses. 
Loss of income:
21. Coming to the aspect of loss of income, the petitioner Ajay claimed that he was a labour and was earning Rs. 20,000/- per month, but due to the accident in question he could not work for 3 months and suffered complete loss of earnings during that period. However, the petitioner has not filed any document to show that he was a labour or that he was earning Rs. 20,000/- per month. Thus, the income of the petitioner will have to be assessed as per the minimum wages. The petitioner has filed on record his Aadhar card bearing no. 2736 2874 3217 as per which he was a resident of Madhya Pradesh and no educational qualification or special skill has been placed on record. Therefore, in the absence of proof of employment and income and considering his address to be of Madhya Pradesh,
the minimum wages for an unskilled labour prevalent in Madhya Pradesh at the time of the accident (on 15.12.2019) i.e. Rs. 7,950/- is taken as the income of the petitioner/ injured Ajay. Therefore, it is held that the monthly income of the petitioner/ injured Ajay at the time of the accident i.e. on 15.12.2019 was Rs. 7,950/-. Further, the petitioner has claimed that he could not go to work for 3 months but there is no proof of the same. However, keeping in view the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, it is held that the petitioner shall be entitled to the Loss of Income for 01 month i.e. Rs. 7,950/-. 
Pain and Suffering:
22. The petitioner/ injured has claim Rs. 50,000/- under the head pain and suffering, however, no justification has been given for claiming such a huge amount. It is true that a particular amount cannot be fixed under the head pain and suffering which could be applicable to all cases as it varies from case to case. Judicial notice can be taken of the fact that since the petitioner has received simple injury, therefore, petitioner must have suffered pain and sufferings owing to the said injuries. 
Considering the nature of injuries suffered by the injured/petitioner, this Tribunal hereby grants compensation of Rs.5,000/- towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner. 
Special Diet:
23. The petitioner has claimed Rs. 49,000/- under the head special diet but there is no cogent evidence on record regarding money spent by the petitioner upon special diet. However, considering the nature of injuries suffered by the injured/petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioner must have spent some money under this head. Hence, this Tribunal hereby grant compensation of Rs. 5,000/- towards expenses incurred on special diet. 
Conveyance charges:
24. The petitioner has claimed Rs. 10,000/- under the head conveyance charges but there is no cogent evidence for the same. However, considering the nature of injuries suffered by the Ajay (I)(Fir414/2019/Burari) vs Sanjay Kachhi (Oic) on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172781374/
9 injured/petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioner must have incurred some expense on conveyance. Hence, this Tribunal hereby grant compensation of Rs. 5,000/- towards conveyance charges. 
Attendant charges:
25. The petitioner/ injured has claimed Rs. 10,000/- under this head, however, there is no cogent evidence on record for the money spent by the petitioner upon an attendant. However, taking into account the injuries suffered by him, Rs. 5,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head of attendant charges. 
Disfiguration:
26. The petitioner has claimed Rs. 50,000/- towards disfiguration, however, he has not filed any document on record to prove the same. Hence, the petitioner/ injured Ajay shall not be entitled to any amount towards disfiguration.

33. The offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1 Sanjay, owned by respondent no. 2, Vichitra Construction and insured with respondent no. 3, Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
34. This being so, it is the case of the insurance company that the insurance company is not liable to indemnify respondent nos. 1 & 2 in the present case as they have violated the terms of the insurance policy. Ld. Counsel for respondent no.3 pointed out that the policy in question was a liability only policy that did not cover the risk of extra passengers. It is also their case that while the policy allowed only one person i.e.
the driver to sit in the offending vehicle, the facts of the case reveal that the deceased Pappu as well as the injured Ajay were standing on the mudguard thus, violating the terms of the insurance policy. Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 3 argued that since the injured was traveling in the offending vehicle as a gratuitous passenger, the liability cannot be fastened upon the insurance company. He has also submitted that Respondent nos. 1 & 2 were also served with the notice issued under Order 12 Rule 8 CPC to produce the original insurance policy of the offending vehicle covering the category of the vehicle as on the date of accident but the same was never produced before it or before this Tribunal. Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 3/Insurance Company examined Ms. Bharti Meena Deputy Manager, Oriental Insurance Co. as R3W1 who proved the dispatch of notice under Order 12 Rule 8 CPC to respondent nos. 1 & 2.
35. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for the petitioners argued that the injured was not a gratuitous passenger and the risk with respect to him is, thus, covered in the insurance policy. She further submitted that the insurance company cannot evade liability only on the ground that there were more number of passengers than allowed. 
36. From the above arguments of Ld. Counsels for the petitioner and respondent no.3, it is clear that there were more persons than authorized on the offending vehicle. Further, the insurance policy is clear that it allowed a seating capacity of only one person.
